title: Putin announces plan to station tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus
body:
On 25 March 2023, Russian President Vladimir Putin said in an interview with Russian state media that Russia would station tactical nuclear weapons in neighbouring Belarus. He framed the move as a warning to the West over its military support for Ukraine, and said it was triggered by Britain's decision to supply Ukraine with armour-piercing rounds containing depleted uranium.

Putin said Russia would keep control of the weapons and that storage facilities would be completed by 1 July. He did not say how many weapons would be sent. He said Russia had helped modernise Belarusian aircraft last year so that they could carry nuclear warheads, that ten such planes were ready, and that Iskander short-range missiles, which Russia had provided to Belarus the previous year, could also launch nuclear weapons. He said Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko had long asked for such weapons as a counter to NATO, and argued that Russia was following U.S. practice of basing nuclear weapons in allied countries.

The U.S. government estimates Russia has about 2,000 tactical nuclear weapons. U.S. National Security Council spokesperson Adrienne Watson said Washington would "monitor the implications" and saw no reason to change its nuclear posture. Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya said the deal underlined the threat posed by Lukashenko's government. Belarus borders three NATO members: Latvia, Lithuania and Poland.
